notes.text: Passports and every tax-free receipt in your carry-on, with every refundable item you bought. The suitcases are already waiting at Haneda T3 with Yamato.
Order at T3: collect suitcases, eat, customs tax-free kiosk, THEN bag drop. Checked bags can't come back out for the kiosk.
Dec 29 is a peak year-end departure day and many shops start shortening hours: don't let the Donki run drift.

stops.summary: Out the door with carry-ons only; the suitcases are already at Haneda.
stops.story: Last checkout, and the lightest one: the big bags went to Haneda T3 by Yamato on the 27th, so today is hands-free until the airport. Do the passport-and-receipt check now, while you're all in one room.
how: Everyone shows their passport and tax-free receipts before leaving.
Toei Shinjuku line from Shinjuku-sanchome to Shinjuku: 22 min door to door, ¥180, or a 10 min taxi.
tips: Keep the Yamato slip somewhere you can find it: you need it at T3.

stops.summary: The hangover-fixing grilled-fish breakfast, charcoal smoke and rice, well under ¥1,000.
stops.story: Shinpachi Shokudo does one thing: a charcoal-grilled fish set (salmon, mackerel or hokke) with rice, miso and pickles, fast and cheap. After a Round1 night that ended at 3, it is the exact reset your body is begging for.
how: Order at the door and take whatever tables free up; 8 usually split across 2–3.
Walk 9 min east through Shinjuku Station to the East Exit for Donki.
tips: It's quick at breakfast, so don't wait for one big table.
Open from 07:00 if anyone wakes early.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: The final Donki raid: KitKats, skincare and snacks, each on your own passport, one receipt.
stops.story: MEGA Don Quijote is the closing ceremony of Japanese shopping: jingle on loop, aisles stacked to the ceiling, every flavour of KitKat that exists. It never closes, so it is the one store year-end can't touch.
how: Each person shops and pays on their own passport.
Get ¥5,000+ ex-tax on one receipt to qualify for the refund.
Everything goes into your carry-on, not your suitcase.
Walk 5 min along Shinjuku-dori to Isetan.
tips: Don't pool purchases across people: the refund is per person, per receipt.
Use the tourist coupon at checkout.
Don't open the snacks: anything eaten in Japan isn't refunded.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Tokyo's most famous basement food hall in New Year rush mode: gift-box sweets for everyone back home.
stops.story: Isetan's depachika is where Tokyo buys its fancy edible gifts: wagashi, high-end sweets in perfect boxes, senbei, sake. Late December it fills with New Year osechi shoppers, packed and loud, a proper year-end scene to end on.
how: Split up and hunt: wagashi, boxed sweets, senbei.
Then Marunouchi, Ginza and Asakusa lines into the Keikyu to Haneda T3: 62 min door to door, ¥650; the first leg leaves Shinjuku-sanchome at 12:34.
tips: Floor hours can differ from the store's: if the food hall isn't open yet, start at Donki.
Boxed sweets stay sealed until home; same tax-free receipt rules as Donki.
A taxi is 31 min if the group is running late.

stops.summary: Grab the suitcases, then a last bowl on T3's 4th-floor Edo street before the paperwork.
stops.story: Edo Koji is a mock Edo-period street on the 4th floor of Terminal 3, all wooden fronts and noren curtains, with gyudon and tonjiru, tonkatsu, oden, udon and ramen side by side. It's landside, so this is your last proper Japanese meal before security.
how: First collect the suitcases at the airport-delivery counter with the Yamato slip.
Up to the 4th floor; split across shops or grab bigger tables.
Walk 1 min to the customs tax-free kiosk.
tips: Shop hours here weren't found: if your pick is closed, the next counter is steps away.
Security is busy on peak days; eat fast.
stops.hours: About 6:30–23:00, varies by shop; terminal open 24 h

stops.summary: Scan passport, show the goods, get the green light: the step that pays back the 10% tax.
stops.story: Since 1 Nov 2026 Japan charges full tax at the till and refunds it at the border. Scan your passport at the kiosk, and green means the refund is approved and paid to the method you registered. Red means a customs inspection, so have the goods at hand.
how: Each person scans their own passport (or uses Visit Japan Web on the airport Wi-Fi).
Have every refundable item to hand: one missing item voids that whole receipt.
Once cleared, pack everything into the checked suitcase and go to bag drop.
tips: Do this BEFORE bag drop: checked bags can't be pulled back for it.
Don Quijote refunds are fee-free unless you take cash at the airport.
Refunds to a card can take 1–2 weeks to land.
stops.hours: Kiosks in the international departure lobby, before bag drop
wishes: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes
